questions.q: Explain the mechanism of the Indian monsoon.

answer.text: The monsoon is driven by the different rates at which land and sea heat and cool. In summer the landmass of India and Central Asia heats up strongly, creating a low-pressure area, while the surrounding oceans remain relatively cool with higher pressure.

This pressure difference, together with the northward shift of the Inter-Tropical Convergence Zone, draws moist south-west winds from the sea onto the land. Arriving as the Arabian Sea and the Bay of Bengal branches, they bring the heavy rains of June to September, an event called the burst of the monsoon.

In winter the land cools faster than the sea, pressure conditions reverse, and dry north-east winds blow out from the land. These pick up moisture over the Bay of Bengal and bring rain to the Tamil Nadu coast.
Jet streams, the heating of the Tibetan Plateau, and the El Nino also affect the monsoon's strength.

answer: Thus seasonal reversal of winds governs India's climate.
